### Execution notes

1. Measure first, per page, whether the object view or Studio already covers it (`AuditLogPage` vs the `sys_audit_log` object view; `DeveloperHubPage` vs the Studio `developer:*` entries).
2. A page that is a duplicate retires here. A page that is kept gets its navigation entry in objectstack `platform-objects`: the claiming seat files that one card in objectstack with `Blocked-by:` from here, so navigation stays the single source of truth.

Claim: PM loop round 2 — `domain:ui` execution seat 4 (serial dispatch, batch 1)

File surface: the objectui half of the triage's execution notes (`5829805557`), for the three orphaned console pages plus one transitive orphan this seat measured.
- `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx`: the `system/audit-log`, `system/ai-approvals`, `developer` and `developer/integrations` routes and their lazy imports only.
- `apps/console/src/pages/system/AuditLogPage.tsx` and `auditLogActions.ts`, `apps/console/src/pages/system/AiPendingActionsPage.tsx`, `apps/console/src/pages/developer/DeveloperHubPage.tsx` and `IntegrationsPage.tsx`, with their tests.
- The console's component-registry files (`apps/console/src/registerDeveloperComponents.tsx`, or one new sibling file in the same shape as `registerApprovalsComponents.tsx`), only to register a KEPT page under a registry key.
- Console docs that name these pages, and one `.changeset/10520-…md`.

Stop on breach; explain in the report.
- ⛔ No edit in objectstack. The framework navigation entries for kept pages are the seat's to file in objectstack, as the triage note says.
- ⛔ `packages/app-shell/**` is untouched. The registry API (`registerAppComponent`) is used as it is.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — measure per page, then retire or register; `priority:p2`: an admin cannot reach the AI approvals queue from the app
Clause-②: yes
Thread-read: 5829805557
Serial constraints cleared:
- The open-PR file lists read 2026-09-25T09:22Z (8 open PRs) show none touching `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx`, `apps/console/src/register*.tsx` or `apps/console/src/pages/{system,developer}/`.
- The live `pm:dispatched` claims of the other seats read at the same time (#10519 `PageView.tsx`, #10500 search seam, #10482 `PagePreview.tsx`, #10442 date faces, #10425 i18n locales) name none of these files. No other `area:devpath` card is in flight.

`Clause-②: yes`. Each page kept gets a new component-registry key, which widens the set of `componentRef` values the console resolves for framework navigation. Each page retired removes a served console route, which narrows it. So the changeset is at least `minor`, and it states any narrowing as breaking in its body (the repo declares no `major`).

### Measured by this seat before claiming (objectui `origin/main`, objectstack `origin/main`)

- The three pages from the card still have only their `Route` declarations as in-app producers.
- **Transitive orphan:** `/apps/:app/developer/integrations` (`IntegrationsPage`) has exactly one in-app producer, a card on `DeveloperHubPage`. It has no registry key: `registerDeveloperComponents.tsx` registers `developer:api-console`, `developer:flow-runs` and `developer:public-forms`, and app-shell registers `developer:packages`. It is in scope because retiring the hub would orphan it too.
- Framework navigation reaches console pages only through `type: 'component'` items whose `componentRef` is a registry key, never a console path. objectstack's `account.app.ts` states it for `approvals:inbox` ("The ref is the component-registry KEY, never a console path"). Studio's developer group already targets `developer:api-console`, `developer:flow-runs`, `developer:public-forms` and `developer:packages`.

### Filed in this act

- **objectstack-ai/objectstack#20142**: the navigation half, per the triage note. It adds `audit:log` to Setup `group_diagnostics`, `ai:approvals` to Setup `group_approvals` (with `requiresService: 'ai'`), and `developer:integrations` to Studio `group_developer`. It carries `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#10520`, and unlocks when objectstack's objectui pin carries this merge.
- **class a:** app-shell's tool-preview "Open in API Console" link points at an app-less `/developer/api-console` URL, which the console redirects to home. The API console also ignores the `path` preset the link carries.

### Acceptance notes (not filed)

- `.claude/skills/objectui-contributor/guides/console-development.md` still lists `DeveloperHubPage`, beside the `SystemHubPage` lines objectui#10507 left. Dropped as a card: it is drift in a governed guide nothing exercises, and the governed surface takes its own PR.
- app-shell's `AppContent.pseudoRouteSegments.test.tsx` keeps a reduced mirror of the host fragment with a stub `developer` route and a `/apps/setup/developer` row. It still passes, because it renders its own stub, but it now mirrors a route the host no longer declares. It is outside this claim; it rides the next PR that touches that file.
- `AuditLogPage.tsx` still gives the old `platform-objects` path for `sys-audit-log.object.ts`, which now lives in `plugin-audit`. This is pre-existing and a comment only.
- `plugin-chatbot`'s `AiPendingActionsInbox` docblock names a `system/ai/pending-actions` console path and a Studio mount, and neither exists. This is a stale comment, dropped.
